newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power slips on warm temps, lower natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power slips on warm temps, lower natgas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices Monday in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) slipped against Friday's levels on warm weather and the ongoing drop in natural gas prices.

Extended forecast showed temperatures in Texas would remain well-above normal into the New Year with day readings in the 60-70 Fahrenheit degree range and night readings in the 30s-50s, about five to 15 10 degrees above seasonal norms.
Swing gas prices in south Texas crashed, down 40 cents to the $2.60 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) mark from Friday's quotes near $3.00.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures fell 25.4 cents at $2.730/mmBtu, extending last week's skid.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday was quoted at $23.50-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), lower than Friday's $24.00-$28.00 for Monday delivery.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Tuesday's heavy load hours was assessed at $22.50-$23.00, weaker than $23.00-$27.00 Friday.
Off-peak, next-day power prices in ERCOT remained depressed due to lackluster demand and ample coal-fired generation, market sources said.
"People have coal (power) all night long," an ERCOT marketer noted.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Tuesday were valued at $9.00-$11.00, down from Friday's $12.00-$13.00 for Monday.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Tuesday's light load hours was notionally quoted at $8.50-$10.50, off from $11.00-$12.00 Friday.
There were little ERCOT forwards activity due to holiday absences and publication of January natgas price indices, market sources said.
